- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 7–14 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% for next 7–14 days.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 3–7 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.  
- If model forecast is significantly below true outcome (e.g., >10% gap) and sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish, expect mean reversion; add 1–3% upward bias for next 5–10 days.  
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% gap) and sentiment is bearish, expect downward correction; reduce forecast by 1–4% for next 5–10 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often underestimates the true mean over 10–15 days; apply a 1–3% upward bias to the first 10–15 days of forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend.
